_doc: SURFACE PARITY REGISTRY. This contract exists because zzop shipped the same bug class more than once: the facade computed a field (configWarnings; git-derived health/recommendations/critical; the run-level, join-scoped MultiAnalyzeOutput::warnings channel, e.g. the parallel-implementation tripwire) but the delivery surface silently dropped it. Every top-level field of AnalyzeOutputView and MultiAnalyzeOutputView (crates/facade/src/output.rs) must get exactly one row below, naming what the delivery surface — the MCP analyze_repo/cross_repo reply, which is the SAME shaped summary the `zzop analyze`/`zzop cross` CLI subcommands print (that is the `zzop` binary, packages/cli-bin; `zzop-mcp` takes NO analysis subcommands at all — bare or `mcp` serves stdio and `version`/`help` are the only other forms) — does with it: 'carry' (forwarded unconditionally), 'carry-conditional' (forwarded only in some shaped/capped/gated form, or only when a precondition holds), or 'omit' (never surfaced by the reply). Every 'omit'/'carry-conditional' row MUST carry a non-empty 'note' explaining why and where the data IS available — which, for anything the shaped reply drops, is either the raw zzop-facade output you get by embedding the engine directly or one of the CLI-only lanes in '_cliOnlyLanes' below (since 2026-07-26 `zzop facts` emits the full CommonIr and the whole cross-layer join, so 'available ONLY via a direct embedding' is no longer true of either — check the row's own note). HISTORICAL NOTE: this registry briefly tracked two JS-CLI render surfaces (a pretty terminal render backed by lib/format.js and a markdown report backed by lib/report.js) across the npm distribution's 2026-07-20 removal-then-restoration; @zzop/cli is now a zero-logic shim that spawns the native `zzop` binary with no render logic of its own, so those two columns are dropped again and only the reply lane remains. SCANNED DELIVERY LANE — what an 'omit' row's note means when it says a field is 'never referenced': the meta-test's haystack is every non-test .rs file under THREE directories, crates/summary/src AND packages/mcp/src AND packages/cli-bin/src (canonical list: mcp_lane_dirs() in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs), minus the `_cliOnlyLanes` implementations declared below. The notes below say 'the scanned delivery lane' and mean all three — never crates/summary/src alone, which would understate the set and let a note read true while packages/mcp/src referenced the field. WHAT AN 'omit' ROW DOES NOT MEAN, and the incident that makes this paragraph load-bearing: 'omit' says THE SHAPED REPLY DOES NOT CARRY THE FIELD, and says nothing whatever about whether anything READS it. The scan behind these notes is narrower than 'does any consumer read this' in two independent ways. (1) MATCHER — it looks for the key literal `"<field>":`, so it sees a re-emission under the field's own name and is structurally blind to a BY-PATH read (`t["output"]["seams"]`, `.get("cache")`, `tree.pointer("/output/ir/loc")`), which is how every consumer of an omitted field in this workspace actually reads it. (2) HAYSTACK — it subtracts every file declared in `_cliOnlyLanes[*].sources`, so a CLI-only lane's consumption is invisible to it BY CONSTRUCTION, and it never scans crates/facade at all, where `query_file`/`query/scan.rs`/`query_coverage` read `ir` by JSON pointer to build the `check_file`/`check_endpoint`/`zzop coverage` answers. On 2026-08-11 a 1.0 readiness reviewer read the four notes that then said an omitted field was reachable 'only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding)', concluded that nine facade fields (`scores`, `scoreMeanings`, `nodes`, `ir`, `folders`, `seams`, `layerCoChurn`, `coChange`, `cache`) reached no surface at all, and proposed DELETING them before 1.0 froze the contract. Re-measured field by field (`grep -rn '\["<field>"\]\|pointer("[^"]*<field>' --include=*.rs crates packages`), SIX of the nine are read by shipped surfaces and three are not; `ir` alone backs two MCP tools and four CLI lanes, so the deletion would have removed live inputs. A document that guards the code was wrong before the code was. Therefore every 'omit' row below now states EITHER its by-path consumers with file and line, OR that a by-path search was run and found none — and 'none' means the search ran, not that a field-name grep came back empty. WHAT GUARDS THIS PROSE, AND WHAT STILL DOES NOT — read this before writing a note. crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs checks the `mcpAnalyzeReply` markers against the real lane, checks that every field of the view has a row, and checks that an 'omit'/'carry-conditional' row's `note` is NON-EMPTY. Since 2026-08-11 it also checks the SHAPE of every 'omit' row's note: the note must contain either a cited consumer written `<file>.rs:<line>` or the literal `grep -rn`, recording that a by-path search was RUN. That is the direct fix for the incident above — the reviewer acted on a sentence that asserted 'nothing reads this' with no evidence attached, and such a sentence now fails the build. It is NOT a truth check and cannot be one: a note that cites a real file:line but describes it wrongly stays green, and so does a note that invents a plausible-looking citation. What the guard converts is UNFALSIFIABLE prose into a claim the next reader can check in one command. Deliberately scoped to 'omit' rows only: a 'carry-conditional' note says the field DOES reach the surface under a stated condition, so it makes no no-consumer claim and has no consumer to cite — demanding one there would produce decorative citations. Nine rows carry the check today. ONE COLUMN, TWO REPLIES — read this before writing a status. `mcpAnalyzeReply` names one delivery LANE that ships two documents, and which one a row speaks about is decided by its ROOT, not by the column: an `analyzeOutputView` row answers for the `analyze_repo`/`zzop analyze` reply, a `multiAnalyzeOutputView` row for the `cross_repo`/`zzop cross` reply. The consequence is a real blind spot and it has been paid for: a PER-TREE field also has a fate inside the cross reply (dropped, carried in a `sources[]` row, or lifted to the join root), and no column states it — while TEST 3's key-literal haystack is the WHOLE lane (crates/summary/src includes cross.rs), so a `carry` satisfied by the join projection reads as though the analyze reply forwarded it. Measured 2026-08-29: `nativeAnalyses` sat at `carry-conditional` on its own row and was absent from every byte of the cross reply, root and `sources[]` alike, with nothing red. Do not fix this by adding a second status column: `registry_surfaces` derives the surface set from the rows and then demands every column on EVERY row, so a cross column would force a nonsense status onto the five `multiAnalyzeOutputView` rows, whose reply the first column already describes. The two mechanisms that DO cover it are `_replyRootKeys` below (top-level keys, machine-checked against a real reply) and behavioural pins in crates/summary/tests; what remains uncovered is the inside of a `sources[]` element, and multiAnalyzeOutputView.trees's note says so. REPLY-ROOT KEYS: a reply key that is not a field of either view can hold no row here (TEST 1/2 pin each root's key set to a facade view) — declare it in `_replyRootKeys` instead, in the same commit, or crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs goes red naming it. A NOTE MAY NOT CONTRADICT ITS OWN COLUMN. If a note spells ``X`, not `Y`` or ``X` rather than `Y`` where both are status tokens, X must BE this row's status; surface_parity.rs enforces it. The rule reads pedantic and was written from an incident: the `nativeAnalyses` and `nativeAnalysesMeaning` rows landed declaring `carry-conditional`, each opening with a paragraph explaining why `carry` is not honest here, and each asserting `carry` further down in the SAME note — a status edit applied to the column and to the first paragraph but not to the last. Nothing was red, because every check on a note was about its emptiness or its citations, never about whether it agreed with the row it sits in. State a status once, in the column, and let the prose explain it. WORKFLOW FOR FUTURE BATCH AGENTS: adding a field to AnalyzeOutputView or MultiAnalyzeOutputView? Add this registry's row for it IN THE SAME COMMIT — crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs's completeness test fails the build otherwise, by design. This file documents TODAY's truth, not an aspiration: a row reflects what the code actually does, not what it should eventually do.

_cliOnlyLanes._doc: Delivery lanes that exist ONLY on the `zzop` CLI, with the reason each has no MCP tool twin, and the .rs files that implement each one's PROJECTION. What `sources` means, precisely, because the subtraction below depends on it: the projection implementation under crates/summary/** — NOT the argv entry points that route to it (packages/cli-bin/src/main.rs and its cli/ module). Those files are deliberately NOT declared, and must not be: they also dispatch lanes that are NOT CLI-only (`analyze`, `cross`, `endpoint`), so subtracting them wholesale would blind the haystack to a real MCP-lane leak in exactly the files where argv meets the shared handlers. The consequence of leaving them in is FAIL-SAFE, which is why it is the right side to err on: if an argv file ever emits an `omit` field's key literal, the guard reads it as an MCP-lane leak and goes RED (a false red someone must then explain), never green. As of 2026-07-26 neither file spells any registry field name as a JSON key literal outside a comment, so nothing is failing today. The PROSE here is documentation (the meta-test's SURFACES list in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs covers `mcpAnalyzeReply` alone) — recorded so a future batch does not 'restore parity' by adding a twin without re-reading why there isn't one. The `sources` arrays, however, ARE machine-read (since 2026-07-26): that meta-test's carry/omit check subtracts exactly those files from the MCP lane it scans, so this block is what defines the boundary between 'a CLI-only lane deliberately emits this' and 'the MCP reply leaks it'. Consequences, both deliberate: a lane that ships without declaring its sources leaves them inside the MCP lane and fails the build the moment it emits an `omit` field (declare the lane, do not rename the key around the guard); and a declared path that no longer resolves is a hard failure, so a moved lane source must update this file in the same commit. The subtraction applies to `carry` rows too — a CLI-only emission must never be what keeps a `carry` row green after the MCP reply stopped forwarding it. NOTE for the `zzop manifest` and `zzop facts` rows below: because both read fields the shaped reply drops, an `omit` row's note can no longer say 'available ONLY via a direct zzop-facade embedding' without qualification — see the `ir` row. Since 2026-08-15 the sources arrays are machine-read in the OTHER direction too (every_non_test_rs_inside_a_declared_lane_module_tree_is_itself_declared, same test file): every non-test .rs inside a declared lane's module tree must itself be declared; a tree's ENTRY file (its mod.rs, or the <name>.rs beside the directory) must stay declared, or its still-declared siblings fail the build naming it; and the honest fix for a genuinely-shared file depends on where the lane lives — under a TEST 3 haystack directory it must MOVE OUT of the lane tree (a declaration would widen the subtraction unverified), while outside the haystack (the zzop explain lane, crates/facade) a declaration subtracts nothing, so classify honestly and declare.

zzop manifest.emits: Identity rows only — provides {kind,key,source}, edges {kind,key,from,to}, buckets {bucket,kind,key,source} — sorted, deduped, UNCAPPED, plus a `tool` fingerprint (zzop_facade::version_string) and per-source {joinContributionZero, degraded}. No file, no line, no root path, no findings.
zzop manifest.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) The manifest is deliberately UNCAPPED, and every MCP reply this repo ships is cap-governed (the token-bomb guard crates/summary/src/output exists for); putting it on that wire would force a choice between breaking that doctrine and capping the one artifact whose whole reason for existing is that the caps make two capped summaries un-diffable above them. (2) The workflow is file-shaped, not conversation-shaped: a manifest earns its keep by being COMMITTED and compared by a later run (the scripts/max-file-lines-baseline.txt model). (3) An agent that wants it can shell out to the same binary — the analysis path is identical.

reads: two `zzop manifest` outputs — no engine, no filesystem beyond the two files
zzop diff.emits: transitions (a key's bucket placement changed — the ranked signal), sources {added, removed, coverageDropped}, and per-relation added/removed for provides/edges/buckets, with `blindnessSuspect` on any removal attributable to a source that lost coverage.
zzop diff.noMcpTwinBecause: It consumes manifests; without a `manifest` twin an agent could not produce its own inputs, so a diff-only tool would be half a surface. Ships with `manifest` or not at all.

reads: trees[].output.gitWindow (presence only — the gate on whether git collection ran)
trees[].output.nodes[].{path,changeCount,churn,authorCount,lastModified} (the dep domain's history axes, read only when that gate says git ran)
trees[].output.scores (presence only — the numbers are deliberately NOT drawn)
zzop graph.emits: TWO FORMATS, selected by `--format`, because its consumer is a renderer rather than a parser. (A) `--format mermaid` (DEFAULT, every domain) — MERMAID TEXT, the one zzop product that is not a JSON document. (B) `--format cosmograph-nodes|cosmograph-links` (`--domain dep` ONLY, a usage error elsewhere) — NDJSON tables for an interactive viewer, one record per line, emitted UNCAPPED: `--top` is refused rather than ignored, because capping exists to keep a DRAWN picture readable and a viewer with zoom does that job itself. Measured on zzop's own tree, mermaid draws 40 of 1165 files where this lane emits all 1165 and all 2154 edges (re-measured 2026-08-01; the figure moves with the repo, so it is illustrative of the RATIO, not a pinned constant), which is the case dep.rs's module doc reserved when it said a large graph is where a different format stays live. Both formats read the SAME uncapped `dep::collect` pass, so they cannot become two answers about one repo. The nodes table carries the axes a viewer styles by; the links table carries `source`/`target`/`endpointsInCycle` — named for the ENDPOINT test it actually runs (both ends are members of some reported cycle), because the reported cycles are flattened into one member set, so a chord inside a cycle and an edge bridging two DIFFERENT cycles both score true without lying on a cycle themselves; the NODE column keeps the name `inCycle`, where claim and computation agree. Nine node columns are STRUCTURAL — `id`/`source`/`path`/`label`/`folder`/`fanIn`/`fanOut`/`degree`/`inCycle`, where `label` is a basename — derived from the graph itself, so every row has them. The rest are MEASURED and ride only when this run measured them: `loc` (from `ir.loc`) and, when `gitWindow` says git collection ran, `changeCount`/`churn`/`authorCount`/`lastModified` (from `nodes[]`). No flag adds or removes a column — a schema that changed per invocation is one no consumer could write against — so what varies is whether a ROW HAS a key. An unmeasured axis is OMITTED, never written as `0`: `churn: 0` would say 'never changed' in the same bytes as 'nobody looked', and a viewer colouring by it would draw the second as the first. That is also why the git axes are gated on `gitWindow` rather than read field-by-field: `nodes[]` is built unconditionally and its counters default to `0`, so on a git-off run every row on the wire carries a perfectly-formed `changeCount: 0`. NDJSON rather than CSV so `serde_json` owns quoting (a path containing a comma cannot silently shift columns). DISCLOSURE GOES TO STDERR for this format, never into the table: stdout is a parseable table and a `%%` census line would be a corrupt row, so the CLI prints the scope/total census on the other stream — and that census also reports how many emitted rows carried each MEASURED axis (`loc on N of M row(s), git history on N of M`), because omitting an unmeasured column is honest but silent: without the count, a reader whose viewer offers no colour-by-churn has nothing to read. A `flowchart LR` with one subgraph per analyzed source and one node per (sourceId, side, kind, key): rectangles for provides, stadiums for consumes, solid arrows for resolved edges, DOTTED arrows for the two non-authoritative relations (an ambiguous consume to each candidate provider, and an edge the linker flagged `lowConfidenceReason`). Each node's bucket rides its LABEL as well as its `classDef` class, so a viewer that drops styling still reads the verdict. SCOPED BY CONSTRUCTION: `--top` caps DRAWN RELATIONS per bucket (default 25, no upper bound — a file/pipe surface, not the capped wire; rows are deduped to distinct relations BEFORE the cap, because a node aggregates call sites and a row-based cap described a picture the reader was not looking at — measured on the OSS corpus, 60 `edges` rows are 4 relations) and `--scope <prefix>` keeps rows whose source id or a site path starts with the prefix; both are disclosed twice, in a `%%` per-bucket drawn/inScope/total-relations census that also publishes the call-site count each aggregates, AND as a visible note node, since a mermaid comment does not survive rendering. NOT emitted, and named in the document's own header rather than left to inference: `crossLayerFindings` (the drift/near-miss VERDICTS — findings ABOUT the join, not members of it; a finding has no node identity here and inventing one would be inventing facts the IR does not have), `hostRekeyCounts` (a counter, not an edge), the warnings/configWarnings/disclosure prose channels, and per-site file/line (nodes AGGREGATE call sites — `zzop facts`/`zzop cross`'s `distinctBucketKeyFirstSites` carry sites). An item with neither `key` nor `raw` is counted as an unlabelable remainder in the census, never guessed at.
zzop graph.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) A diagram is a terminal/file act — `zzop graph ./api ./web > join.mmd` then a renderer — the same file- and pipe-shaped lane `manifest` and `facts` argued for; an agent that wants the picture shells out to the same binary for identical bytes. (2) The shaped answers already exist on the MCP wire: `cross_repo` carries the same buckets as counts, keys and sites, which is what a PROGRAM reasons over, while a flowchart is for a human eye. A tool twin would put the same data on two surfaces under two different shaping rules — the exact drift class this registry exists to prevent. (3) Since the cosmograph format landed, this lane also emits an UNCAPPED table — 1165 nodes and 2154 edges on zzop's own tree — which is the same argument `manifest` and `facts` make, only now it applies to a lane whose reader is explicitly a HUMAN at a viewer rather than an agent in a conversation. Putting it on the cap-governed wire would force capping the one output whose reason for existing is that it is not capped.

zzop facts.emits: The whole post-assembly FACT SUBSTRATE, UNCAPPED and verbatim: `{tool, config, configWarnings, trees[{sourceId, coverage, warnings, commonIr}], crossLayer, warnings, disclosure}`. The consumer half of the custom-rule extension point — zzop emits what it knows and a user's own program decides what is a problem. It executes nothing (no process spawn) and ingests nothing (no findings channel back in). NOT emitted: zzop's own `findings`/`crossLayerFindings` (verdicts, not facts — a rule author computes their own, and carrying ours would put the same data on two surfaces under two different caps), and `AttributeStore` (the one post-assembly fact whose CONTAINER is not already a serialized wire shape; emitting it would freeze a NEW shape, which this repo's projection-contract bar gates behind a consuming rule existing first). KEY NAMING: the per-tree IR rides under `commonIr`, not `ir` — a design choice, and (since 2026-07-26) no longer a guard workaround: the meta-test enforcing the `ir` row's `omit` status now subtracts this lane's `sources`, so either spelling would pass it. `commonIr` camel-cases the exact type a rule author has to look up to read the block (`zzop_core::CommonIr`, field list in docs/modules/facade.md) and stays greppable inside a consumer's own codebase, which a two-letter key that is a substring of `circular`/`directory`/`require` is not. The cost is one mapping to remember, because a direct zzop-facade embedding spells the same block `ir` — stated in the `ir` row below so a reader diffing the two surfaces meets it there.
zzop facts.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) The output is deliberately UNCAPPED and grows with tree size, while every MCP reply this repo ships is cap-governed (crates/summary/src/output) — the same argument the `ir` row already makes for the analyze reply, only stronger: `ir` alone measured 107x the shipped reply on zzop's own tree and `facts` carries the whole join on top. The main MCP consumer is an AI agent, so output size is a direct context cost. (2) The consumer is a PROGRAM, not a conversation: the workflow is `zzop facts ./api ./web > facts.json && ./my-rule facts.json`, a terminal/CI act. (3) An agent already has the shaped answers it usually wants (join buckets, check_endpoint); `facts` exists for the case those cannot serve, which is precisely the case that is not a conversation. An agent that genuinely wants it can shell out to the same binary for the identical answer.

reads: trees[].output.ir.symbols + trees[].output.ir.dep (structural membership; non-empty dep source entries additionally feed the per-extension inDepGraph count)
zzop_engine::rule_sightlines (compiled-in per-rule sightline declarations — CAPABILITY input, code not run)
zzop_engine::framework_recognizers (compiled-in per-parser framework declarations — CAPABILITY input, code not run)
zzop coverage.emits: the aggregate-visibility view: per-extension dispatch table (structural/lexicalOnly/degraded, plus inDepGraph — files of the extension with at least one resolved outgoing dep edge, the per-extension import-resolution sparsity baseline), per-tree blindSpots (class-aware cross of each declared rule sightline with the tree's structural extensions) with blindSpotBasis (what the cross was computed from AND what it EXCLUDED) and the top-level blindSpotMeaning legend, the per-tree unreadExtensions cell naming each PRINCIPAL filetype no structural parser read — the population that cross structurally cannot contain, since a language with no parser never becomes a structural extension and so vanishes from the very list a reader checks for blindness, with its own top-level unreadExtensionMeaning legend, the top-level frameworkRecognizers table ({framework, extensions, emits} rows verbatim from the compiled-in declarations, uncrossed with any tree — emits bound to each adapter's own io construction SIDE AND KIND, so the db kind is spelled io.provides:db-table for table DECLARATIONS and io.consumes:db-table for queries against one, and extensions bound to the dispatcher) with its frameworkRecognizerMeaning legend — the build-capability answer to "does this tool know my stack?" that previously had no user surface, per-tree warnings forwarded verbatim, the census with joinVisibility as COUNTS (provides, consumesKeyed, consumesUnresolved) plus a meaning — naming that only an io-fact-contributing overlay restores join visibility, and that a key is a precondition for joining rather than proof of one; no rate is derived, because a quotient reads the same at 1-of-1 as at 400-of-440, the per-tree ioChannels cell (extracted: one row per read io kind, PRESENT EVEN AT ZERO, so one filled channel cannot vouch for another empty one the way the kind-agnostic joinContributionZero does; zeroExtraction: the CAPABILITY x MEASURED cross naming each (channel, extension) a SINGLE recognizer row of this build names both halves of and whose extraction on this tree came back 0, its recognizers[] being the complete set for that exact pair so the 0 is relative to those alone, restricted to extensions that are a PRINCIPAL share of the structurally-read population (the same floor unreadExtensions applies, against its own denominator) so a rounding-error filetype is ABSENT rather than cleared — a COVERAGE FACT keyed on the tree's structural extension mix rather than on recognizing a framework by name, so a framework no hand-kept vocabulary lists still produces the row), a conditional walkNote when files under a .git/ segment were walked (the otherTrees convention: absent means none were), and the unmeasured axes as a FIELD — by ruling (2026-07-31) no single score exists in the schema
zzop coverage.noMcpTwinBecause: an authoring/ops aggregate over the whole tree. The MCP agent surface already carries the per-file half (check_file) and the per-run census rides every analyze reply; an agent wanting the aggregate can ask analyze_repo and read coverage. If agent demand for the AGGREGATE arrives, promote then — the core (zzop_facade::query_coverage_json) is host-neutral by construction, so the twin is a dispatch entry away.

reads: nothing from a run — the bundled DSL pack data compiled INTO the binary
zzop explain.emits: One rule's compiled-in data as human-readable lines, or a guided Err naming what the id actually is (a native analysis id, a pack id, an output field id, an ambiguous bare id, or unknown).
zzop explain.noMcpTwinBecause: It answers from data that is already ON the MCP wire as a whole: the `rule-catalog` contract resource carries every shipped rule id with its prose, so an agent looks a rule up by reading one document rather than by calling a tool per id. The subcommand exists because a TERMINAL user wants one rule, not the catalog. Declared here — even though its projection lives in crates/facade rather than crates/summary — because the one-audience fact is what both consumers of this block need: crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/host_vocabulary.rs's contract 16 subtracts these files when it checks that shared crates name no CLI-only vocabulary, and naming `zzop explain` inside the `zzop explain` lane is correct, not a leak. NOT declared, deliberately: `zzop init`. Its only implementation is the argv entry point (packages/cli-bin/src/cli/run.rs), which this block's `_doc` forbids declaring, and the bytes it writes are a two-audience contract resource that MCP `resources/read` serves as well.

buildScriptPaths.note: The tree's own package.json `scripts` path tokens, resolved against the walked file set and sorted (zzop_engine::AnalyzeOutput::build_script_paths). Omitted from the reply but NOT unconsumed — it is the third input to the shaped reply's finding ORDER: `crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs:67` reads it by key and `crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs:73` hands it to `output::shape_findings`, whose deployment-role tier sorts findings on these files after every production and test-path finding, ahead of severity rather than within one band (`crates/summary/src/output/deployment_role.rs` is the judgment). Measured, not assumed: `grep -rn 'buildScriptPaths' --include=*.rs crates packages` returns the producer field (`crates/facade/src/output.rs:71`), the facade's own key-set and value pins (`crates/facade/src/analyze_tests.rs`), exactly ONE runtime read (`crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs:67`), and doc-comment mentions in the shaper — no other surface, no CLI-only lane, no query core. The by-path search matters here for the reason `_doc` gives: a key read via `output_view["buildScriptPaths"]` is a bracket index, not a struct field, so a field-name scan alone would have called this row unconsumed. What a reader sees of it is therefore the `findings.buildPaths` disclosure, which carries the COUNT and the sentence; the path list itself would be a second, larger copy of a fact the ordering already applied. Available whole via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding). ALWAYS serialized at the facade boundary, `[]` included: every tree outside the npm ecosystem declares no build script by construction, and an empty array is what separates 'walked, declared nothing' from 'an engine build that does not report this'.

cache.note: Cache PROVENANCE. Was `omit` until 2026-08-17 on the reading that hit/miss counts are an internal performance diagnostic; the counts are also the only thing in the reply that separates a RECOMPUTED finding list from one REPLAYED off disk, which made a manufactured zero (a hand-edited cache entry, measured with the credential still in the source) unanswerable from the reply alone. The shaper now forwards a projection — {hitFiles, missFiles, fileCount, meaning} via `output::cache_signal` — not the raw `CacheStatsView`, and only when a cache was in play, so a run with caching off grows no key (absent, never null, same contract as architecture/ruleTimings). `--profile-rules` still reads `output.cache.hits` by JSON path for its own disclosure; the two derive from one field rather than one of them re-deriving it.

coChange.note: Never forwarded on the shaped reply, but NOT unconsumed: the shipped CLI lane `zzop graph --domain cochange` reads `output.coChange` BY JSON PATH (`crates/summary/src/graph/cochange.rs:80`), which no field-name scan shows — that file is a declared `_cliOnlyLanes` source (subtracted from the haystack) and the read is a path index rather than a key literal, so the scan is blind to it twice over (see `_doc`). The omission is for the same reason `ir` is omitted and NOT because it is bulky: the edge list is UNBOUNDED in tree size (one entry per surviving file pair — 972 on zzop's own tree, `zzop graph --domain cochange --top 100000 | grep -c ' --- '`), while the shipped reply is capped. AVAILABILITY: the CLI-only `zzop graph --domain cochange` lane draws it, capped by `--top` and with that cap plus the two upstream filters disclosed inside the document itself; a direct zzop-facade embedding yields the whole array. NOT interchangeable with `layerCoChurn`: that field keeps only pairs CROSSING an architectural layer, so it cannot answer 'what changes together' inside one module, which is this field's whole subject. A consumer must also keep `null` and `[]` apart — `null` means git was inactive (nothing measured), `[]` means it was measured and no pair survived.

critical.note: Only the top 3 paths (the engine's own SIZE-WEIGHTED blast-radius ranking: blast_radius * ln(loc+2), with blast radius as the tie-break — crates/metrics/src/criticality.rs::compute_criticality) ride the compact `architecture.criticalTop` summary (crates/summary/src/analyze/architecture.rs::architecture_summary). This row said 'blast-radius ranking' until 2026-07-31, which invited a consumer to reproduce the three paths by sorting `critical` on `blastRadius`; that sort is a DIFFERENT order whenever two hubs of similar blast differ in size. The full CriticalFile list (with contributing metrics, in this same order) is available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

degraded.note: The raw degraded-path list is capped (DEFAULT_DEGRADED_LIMIT=50) with an explicit `degradedTruncated` disclosure when capped (`crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs:39,108` — the cap and the `degradedTruncated` insert; cited with lines because a bare filename is not a claim a later reader can check, which is the rule `_doc` now states and `surface_parity.rs` now holds) — `coverage.degraded` already carries the full uncapped count. The full uncapped per-file list is available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

disclosure.note: Carried as a FOLD since 2026-07-29 (crates/summary/src/output/disclosure.rs): the reply gets the registry's counts plus a pointer (`zzop contract disclosure-classes` / `zzop://contract/disclosure-classes`), never the ~10.6KB of run-invariant prose. The full text is available from the contract lane on both surfaces and, verbatim, from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane.

findings.note: Shaped via output::shape_findings into {total, bySeverity, byRule, byRuleMeaning, shown (deployment role desc, then severity-desc, capped at DEFAULT_FINDINGS_LIMIT=50 unless the caller supplies `limit`), truncated?, testPaths?, buildPaths?, note?, ruleMessages?, ruleMessagesMeaning?} — never the raw findings array verbatim. Each entry of `shown` carries `message` as a string always; a text that MORE THAN ONE shown finding carries AND whose folding removes more bytes than the pointer, the `messageRef` field and the table cost to add is stored once in a sibling `ruleMessages` object (`{key: text}`, keyed by rule id, `<ruleId>#2` for a rule's later distinct texts) and those findings carry `messageRef` holding the key plus a short pointer `message`. The gate is net bytes, not repetition, and it is applied per text: a short message repeated inside one reply stays inline while a long one beside it folds, because the pointer plus the field plus the row cost about 260 bytes a finding and 45 of the 118 shipped messages are cheaper carried twice than folded once. Both `ruleMessages` and its legend `ruleMessagesMeaning` are additive-only — absent, never empty — so a reply whose every message is unique is byte-identical to what it was before the fold existed. The fold runs on `shown` AFTER the cap, is lossless (`crates/summary/src/output/rule_prose.rs`), and moves no count: resolve with `ruleMessages[finding.messageRef]`, never by parsing the pointer sentence, which `VERSIONING.md` keeps explicitly outside the compatibility surface while freezing the field names. `truncated` is {shown, totalMatching, severitiesNotShown, hint}: `severitiesNotShown` ({counts, meaning}, always present inside `truncated`) names the severity bands the cut removed OUTRIGHT, counted over the post-filter set the cap was applied to, because role-first ordering can push a whole `critical` band past the cap while `bySeverity` keeps counting it (cal.com at --limit 1000: `critical: 6` beside 1000 rows carrying none). The `hint` drops "raise the limit" at limit == MAX_LIMIT, where a larger value is a usage error rather than a remedy. `note` is the zero-match disclosure for the `rule` and `severity` filters, present only when a filter was given and matched nothing (both notes join into the one key when both fired): an empty `shown` from a real-but-quiet rule and an empty `shown` from a TYPO are the same bytes without it. The two path keys are ordering DISCLOSURES, not filters: shipped code sorts before test paths, which sort before build surface, ahead of severity rather than within one tier (crates/summary/src/output/deployment_role.rs), and each demoted tier publishes its own full-set count. Both are additive-only — absent, never `{count: 0}` — so a tree with no test or build surface pays no bytes for the axis.

folders.note: FolderAggregates is never forwarded — no folder-level rollup rides the reply — and, re-measured 2026-08-11 with the by-path search the field-name scan cannot do, it is GENUINELY UNCONSUMED: `grep -rn 'folders' --include=*.rs crates packages` finds the producer (`crates/facade/src/output.rs:99,160`, `crates/metrics/src/aggregates.rs`) and one unrelated doc-comment mention (`crates/summary/src/graph/model.rs:6`), and NO key literal, bracket-path or `pointer()` read on any surface — not in the shaped reply, not in a CLI-only lane, not in the facade's own query cores. This row is therefore one of the three (with `layerCoChurn` and `scoreMeanings`) where 'omit' and 'nothing reads it' happen to coincide; do not generalize that to the other six omit rows, which DO have by-path consumers. Available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding); unlike nodes/scores/seams/coChange, which the `zzop graph` domains read by path, and unlike health/recommendations/critical, which get a compact `architecture` cameo, folders reaches nothing at all.

gitWindow.note: Forwarded verbatim via a `.get()`-defensive check, only when the key is present (crates/summary/src/analyze/mod.rs) — the facade itself always serializes this field (null when git did not run), but the forwarding step is conditional on presence rather than being an unconditional index. The always-present field is available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

health.note: Gated on `health` being non-null (git signals ran this tree). `contributors` (the per-metric breakdown, including the rows naming which metrics were UNMEASURED) never reaches the reply — the full health object is available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding). What does ride `architecture` is `pain` PLUS its denominator: `painMeasuredWeight`/`painTotalWeight` (mirroring `health.measuredWeight`/`totalWeight`) and a `painMeaning` sentence. That trio is deliberate and is the one place this contract lets a composite scalar cross to a host surface: `pain` renormalizes over the metrics that had a population, so quoting it without saying how much of the metric table was measurable reproduces exactly the folded-single-score failure `queryCoverage` forbids. Before 2026-08-08 only the bare scalar crossed, and because an unmeasurable metric scores 100 and contributed no pain, a tree zzop could see LESS of scored better. `pain` is null (never 0) when nothing was measurable.

ir.note: The full CommonIr (dep graph, per-file tags/loc/symbols, and `ir.io`'s provide/consume lists) never rides any MCP/`zzop-mcp` reply. The reason is UNBOUNDEDNESS, not bulk: `ir` grows in proportion to tree size while the shipped reply is capped (findings <= DEFAULT_FINDINGS_LIMIT and friends), so which one is bigger depends entirely on the tree — measured, `ir` is 0.68x the shipped reply on a 52-file tree and 107x on zzop's own. An earlier wording here read 'deliberate token-shaping decision', which invited the false gloss that `ir` is always too large; the honest statement is that a capped reply stays predictable for an agent's context budget and an uncapped `ir` does not. An AI consumer gets the io facts it usually wants through the cross-layer join buckets / check_endpoint instead of the raw `ir` block. AVAILABILITY (changed 2026-07-26 — this row is `omit` for the MCP reply only, it is no longer 'MCP-omitted therefore embed-only'): the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane emits the WHOLE block verbatim, under the key `trees[].commonIr` — same data, different spelling, deliberately (see `_cliOnlyLanes` for the lane, its no-MCP-twin judgment, and the naming rationale); the CLI-only `zzop manifest` lane reads `ir.io.provides` alone and projects it to identity rows — kind/key/source, never the file/line/symbol/body detail; and a direct zzop-facade embedding still yields it under its own `ir` key. CONSUMERS BEYOND THOSE TWO LANES, added 2026-08-11 because their absence here is what let a reviewer read this row as 'nothing uses `ir`': five more shipped surfaces read INTO this block by JSON path or pointer without ever emitting it whole, which no field-name grep shows. On the MCP wire itself, `check_file` reads `/output/ir/loc`, `/output/ir/symbols` and `/output/ir/dep` (`crates/facade/src/query_file.rs:186,210,217,234` and `crates/facade/src/query_file/facets.rs:8,17,70`) and `check_endpoint` reads `ir.io` (`crates/facade/src/query/scan.rs:38`) — so `omit` here means the RAW BLOCK is not forwarded, never that the MCP surface is ignorant of it. On the CLI, `zzop coverage` reads the same FOUR sub-paths (`io` joined on 2026-08-20, so a file whose parser projects io and nothing else — `.sql`, `.prisma` — counts as structurally read) through `zzop_facade::query_coverage_json` (`crates/facade/src/query_coverage.rs:104,113,121,136`), and `zzop graph` reads `ir.dep` (`crates/summary/src/graph/dep.rs:133`), `ir.loc` (`crates/summary/src/graph/cochange.rs:74`, `crates/summary/src/graph/dep/node.rs:61`) and `ir.io.provides` (`crates/summary/src/graph/posture.rs:85`). Counting them, `ir` is the MOST-consumed field in this registry, omit rows and carry rows alike — the opposite of an orphan, and the field whose deletion would have cost the most.

layerCoChurn.note: Never forwarded, and — re-measured 2026-08-11 with the by-path search the field-name scan cannot do — GENUINELY UNCONSUMED: `grep -rn 'layerCoChurn\|layer_co_churn' --include=*.rs crates packages` hits only the PRODUCER side (`crates/engine/src/analyze/assemble/metrics.rs`, `crates/engine/src/output.rs:59`) and the capability diagnostic that names it as git-gated (`crates/engine/src/analyze/diagnostics/capability.rs:24`) — no key literal, no bracket-path read, no `pointer()` read on any surface, CLI-only lanes and the facade's query cores included. Available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding). NOT interchangeable with `coChange` in the other direction either: that sibling IS read by a shipped lane (`zzop graph --domain cochange`) while this one is read by nothing, so the two rows say 'omit' for the same reason but have opposite consumption facts — see that row.

nativeAnalyses.note: STATUS NOTE: `carry-conditional` rather than `carry`, and the reason is about the GUARD, not about the field — it is forwarded under its own name on every reply this build produces. `carry` is asserted by one mechanism only, `surface_parity.rs`'s grep for the literal `"<field>":`, which that test's own doc says a key inserted by name (`summary.insert("nativeAnalyses".to_string(), ..)`) is invisible to in both directions; the shipped `carry` rows satisfy it incidentally, from cross.rs's `json!` rows. Contorting the shaper to plant a substring would make the code worse and prove nothing extra. `carry-conditional` is also literally accurate: the forward is `.get()`-gated so an older engine/facade degrades to omission rather than a JSON `null`, exactly `packsLoadedMeaning`'s lane. It is listed in crates/summary/src/analyze/tests.rs's CONDITIONAL_UNDER_ITS_OWN_NAME, and the enforcement it trades up to is BEHAVIORAL rather than textual: `the_shaped_reply_carries_the_native_analyses_disclosure_and_its_legend` runs the shaper and asserts both keys with their content. NOW THE FIELD ITSELF: the native counterpart of `packsLoaded`: {registered, disabled, reportedInCrossLayerFindings} — how many native analyses this build registers and which of them could not have keyed this reply's findings map, split by CAUSE. Added 2026-08-28 after a whole-catalog audit found 106 of 184 catalogued ids absent from every reply and no channel able to say why; the DSL half of that question was already answered by packsLoaded's `didNotRun`/`zeroAdmissionRules`, and the native half had no channel at all. UNCONDITIONAL IN SUBSTANCE — which is a different question from the STATUS above, and conflating the two is what left this row contradicting itself for a day (it declared `carry-conditional`, opened with the STATUS NOTE explaining why, and then asserted `carry` twice further down; a half-finished edit, and no guard held the prose against its own column). The FIELD is unconditional: the object is a statement about the BUILD rather than about the caller's request, so unlike ruleOverridesApplied there is no 'nothing was asked' state, and both inner lists serialize even when empty — the deliberate break with `zeroAdmissionRules`'s skip-if-empty convention, because a channel whose population is 'what I found' reports nothing on a clean run in bytes indistinguishable from one that never ran. Both lists are DERIVED per run from the registrations themselves (`zzop_engine::register_all_native` for the population, `zzop_rules_cross_layer::register_native_analyses` for the cross-layer subset) and gated through `zzop_core::is_enabled`, the same call the evaluator makes, so no count here can drift from the registry or from the gate; the floor that stops a broken derivation reading as 'everything was evaluated' is crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/native_analyses.rs. THE JOIN LANE, added 2026-08-29: the same roster now also rides the `cross_repo`/`zzop cross` reply at its ROOT, derived for the run the join actually gated (crates/summary/src/cross/native_analyses.rs) and declared in `_replyRootKeys.cross_repo` below, because a per-tree field lifted to the join root is not a `multiAnalyzeOutputView` field and so can hold no row of its own. It carries a FOURTH key there, `zeroInCrossLayerFindings` — the population minus the keys of `crossLayerFindings.byRule` — which only that reply can compute, and its legend forks: in a per-tree reply `reportedInCrossLayerFindings` means `run the join`, while in the join reply those analyses ARE the channel being read. Measured before the fix: the cross reply carried the roster nowhere (not at the root, not on any of nine `sources[]` rows) while its own byRule held 18 keys against a 27-analysis roster. Pinned behaviourally by crates/summary/tests/cross_native_analyses.rs, including a two-directional canary (one tree disables one id; it must leave the population and appear under `disabled`). Forwarded to the MCP/CLI shaped reply by crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs, which is the lane the defect was measured on: `zzop analyze` over each of nine single-tree corpus configs reported zero `cross-layer/*` keys while the cross-layer join over the SAME nine configs produced 975 findings on 9 trees of 9.

nativeAnalysesMeaning.note: Same status and same reason as its sibling row above — see that note for why `carry` is not the honest label for a key the shaper inserts by name. The legend for `nativeAnalyses`: build-constant sentences keyed `registered`, `disabled`, `reportedInCrossLayerFindings` and `everythingElse` (the residual class with no field of its own, precisely because it is the case where absence IS the verdict). The residual sentence used to say that absence from `findings` is a measured zero FULL STOP, which its own neighbour `registered` contradicted for two registration classes — score-gating ids that emit no finding at all, and umbrella ids whose findings arrive under finer `schema/<label>` ids; it now carves those out by name and defers to `registered` for their description, pinned by a position test in crates/facade/src/output/native_analyses_legend.rs. The JOIN reply carries a five-key sibling of this legend (crates/summary/src/cross/native_analyses.rs): `registered` and `disabled` are READ FROM THIS FILE's constants (zzop_facade::NATIVE_ANALYSES_REGISTERED_MEANING / _DISABLED_MEANING, the latter with one clause appended about the join's exclude-only gate) so the two replies cannot disagree about their own denominator, while the other sentences are lane-specific by design. Same sibling-key shape and same reason as `packsLoadedMeaning`, and the same reason this repo pairs every machine field with a meaning: an auditor reading counts alone called the nearest existing channel a pointer rather than a statement. UNCONDITIONAL IN SUBSTANCE, unlike its packsLoaded twin — packsLoaded can legitimately be empty, while every build registers native analyses, so this legend is written on every reply. That is a fact about the FIELD; the `carry-conditional` in the column is a fact about the GUARD, and this note asserted the second from the first until 2026-08-29 (see the sibling row for the same half-finished edit and the rule that now holds it). Forwarded beside the object itself in crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs; the two keys move together, since numbers without the legend are exactly the half already judged insufficient.

nodes.note: The FileNode list is never forwarded (`architecture.criticalTop` derives from `critical`, a separately-ranked view, not from `nodes`). The full per-file node list (tagCounts, loc, every metric) rides the raw zzop-facade output AND the shipped CLI lane `zzop graph --domain dep`, which reads `output.nodes` by JSON path (`crates/summary/src/graph/dep/node.rs:94`) — including the cosmograph formats.

packsLoaded.note: Rows gained `didNotRun` and `filesInScopeIfEnabled` on 2026-08-26, both conditional and both ABSENT on a pack that ran — an ungated run's array is byte-identical to what it was before. `filesInScope` became conditional in the same change (present exactly when the pack ran); see the facade table and `zzop_engine::PackLoaded`'s own doc for the measured misreading that forced the split. Nothing about which packs load or run changed, only what the row says about them.

packsLoadedMeaning.note: The legend for `packsLoaded`: an object of build-constant sentences keyed `row`, `filesInScope` and `zeroAdmissionRules`, plus `didNotRun` only when a pack really was gated off (deliberately spelled as a key list rather than a brace literal — a brace literal here sits inside the window `packages/mcp/tests/nested_reply_shape_prose.rs` scans for the SIBLING `packsLoaded` anchor, whose name this one contains as a prefix, and would be judged against that field's wire shape). Added 2026-08-26, when an auditor found this reply's one numeric channel with no `meaning` beside it and two readings of `zeroAdmissionRules` whose implications are opposite. `carry-conditional` on BOTH ends: the facade omits the key when no DSL pack loaded (an empty roster has no entries to explain, and `packsLoaded: []` already carries that fact), and the MCP lane forwards it through a `.get()`-gated `summary.insert` in crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs — the gate is what preserves the omission instead of turning it into JSON `null`, exactly as `ruleOverridesApplied`'s does. `cross_repo` carries ONE merged copy at the reply root rather than repeating it in each `sources[]` row (crates/summary/src/cross.rs); the merge is order-independent because every value is the same build constant, and the `didNotRun` entry appears there when ANY tree gated a pack. Made visible to this registry by a third facade pin, crates/facade/src/analyze_tests.rs's `analyze_json_top_level_key_set_with_packs_loaded_is_pinned_exactly` — the two older pins load no pack and so structurally cannot see this key, the same blind spot `ruleOverridesApplied` closed in 2026-07-26; surface_parity.rs derives its pin union by NAME shape, so that new pin joined it with no edit here.

recommendations.note: Only recommendations[0] (the top ROI-ranked entry) rides `architecture.topRecommendation` ({id, severity, topItem}) — remaining recommendations and each one's full items list are available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

ruleOverridesApplied.note: The one CONDITIONALLY-PRESENT top-level field: the facade omits the key entirely (never an empty object) when the caller requested no `disabledRules`/`severityOverrides`/`packsOnly` (the `only` member joined the payload in v0.29.0, when a release audit found the pack allowlist suppressing findings with no positive acknowledgement anywhere on the wire) — see `zzop_engine::RuleOverridesApplied`'s own doc and crates/facade/src/analyze_tests.rs's `analyze_json_omits_rule_overrides_applied_when_nothing_was_requested`. When present it is forwarded WHOLE and uncapped (bounded by the caller's own request size, same as packsLoaded) through a `.get()`-gated `summary.insert` in crates/summary/src/analyze/mod.rs — the gate is what preserves the omission instead of turning it into JSON `null`. `cross_repo` carries it too, inside each `sources[]` row (see multiAnalyzeOutputView.trees's note). Row added 2026-07-26: this field had NO row here until then, because the single pinned key-set fixture surface_parity.rs reads never requested an override, so the completeness test could not see the field at all; crates/facade/src/analyze_tests.rs now carries a second pin with an override requested, and surface_parity.rs unions the two.

ruleTimings.note: Per-rule wall-clock timing. Forwarded by `analyze/shape.rs` ONLY when the run was instrumented, and instrumentation is reachable from the `zzop` CLI alone (`--profile-rules`, which sets the `profileRules` request field): the facade always serializes this key, `null` when profiling was off, and the shaper gates on the VALUE being an array so an unprofiled reply grows no field at all. No MCP tool argument turns it on, so in practice the `analyze_repo` reply never carries it today — `carry-conditional` rather than `carry` because that is a property of which arguments the MCP surface offers, not of this shaper, and rather than `omit` because the field name IS spelled as a forwarded key literal in the shared lane. Was `omit` until 2026-08-02, when the capability (EngineConfig::profile_rules) was wired to a user-reachable surface for the first time; its only caller before that was crates/engine/examples/bench.rs. The forwarded object carries its own `meaning` string disclosing that cache hits contribute no timing.

scoreMeanings.note: One sentence per `scores` key, shipped beside the numbers it explains (added 2026-08-04). Follows `scores` exactly: present when git signals ran, absent otherwise, and omitted from the MCP reply for the same reason `scores` is — that reply forwards only the DERIVED architecture summary, so a legend for numbers it does not carry would explain nothing. Reachable ONLY on the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding). This row said 'and the `zzop analyze` CLI form' until 2026-08-11, which contradicted its own `omit` marker: `zzop analyze` prints `zzop_summary::analyze_summary_with` (`packages/cli-bin/src/cli/analysis.rs`, `run_analyze`), the SAME shaped summary the MCP reply is — that identity is this registry's founding premise, stated in `_doc` — so a field omitted from the reply is omitted from `zzop analyze` too, and a reader who ran the CLI expecting the legend found nothing. Re-measured 2026-08-11 including by-path reads: `grep -rn 'scoreMeanings\|score_meanings' --include=*.rs crates packages` hits only the producer (`crates/facade/src/output.rs:91,150`, `crates/metrics/src/scores/meanings.rs`) and its own pins, so no CLI-only lane and no facade query core reads it either — GENUINELY UNCONSUMED, one of the three such rows (with `folders` and `layerCoChurn`). Note the asymmetry with the field it explains and do not 'fix' it by deleting either: `scores` IS read by a shipped lane, but that lane (`zzop graph --domain risk`, `crates/summary/src/graph/risk.rs:77`) only CENSUSES how many trees computed scores and deliberately draws none of the numbers (`risk.rs:181` prints a 'NOT drawn' line saying so), so it needs no legend. Why it exists at all: four of the then-seventeen score keys were bare acronyms whose expansion lived only in Rust doc-comments — two of them (`sfc`, `fsd`) have since been renamed on the wire to `fileSizeCompliance`/`featureSlicedDesign` because their letters named the wrong thing, and `sdp` stays abbreviated because it abbreviates a proper name (`lod`, the other such key, was removed with its score on 2026-08-08 for never having measured anything) — a name survey measured zero occurrences of "Stable Dependencies Principle" across docs/ and site/ — so a consumer holding `scores.sdp = 41.2` had no vocabulary on any surface. Same self-describing-reply device as `verdictMeaning`, and the same reason: a documentation table would give one fact a second owner. Definitions have one owner, `zzop_metrics::SCORE_MEANINGS`, whose completeness is pinned against serde's own key set. The completeness pin runs in BOTH directions, so a sentence can neither be missing for a live score nor outlive a removed one.

scores.note: The raw per-metric Scores struct (which feeds health/recommendations) is never forwarded directly — only the DERIVED `health.pain` and top `recommendations[0]` reach the reply via the architecture summary. The MCP reply forwards only the derived pair; the full per-metric table rides the raw zzop-facade output AND the shipped CLI lane `zzop graph --domain risk`, which reads `output.scores` by JSON path to census how many trees computed them (`crates/summary/src/graph/risk.rs:77`). Its legend rides beside it as `scoreMeanings` (see that row). Since 2026-08-08 every score also carries the POPULATION it scored over in the same object (`featureSlicedDesign.layerClassifiedImports`, `busFactor.total`, `mainSequence.classifiedFiles`, ...): a population of 0 is the never-measured signal, because every per-metric formula returns 100 on an empty population and the denominator is the only thing that separates "judged everything, all clean" from "found nothing to judge". The same ruling removed `typeSafety` and `lod`, whose input channels had no producer anywhere in the build and which therefore published a perfect score on every run ever made. NOTE the parity consequence: because this row is `omit`, the MCP reply carries no per-metric population at all — which is exactly why `architecture` now forwards `pain`'s own denominator (`painMeasuredWeight`/`painTotalWeight`), see the `health` row.

seams.note: SeamCandidate list is never forwarded on the MCP reply, but it is NOT unconsumed: `zzop graph --domain risk` draws it, reading `output.seams` by JSON path (`crates/summary/src/graph/risk.rs:91`). The scan that reports it as unreferenced matches Rust field access and cannot see a JSON-path read.

trees.note: cross_repo reshapes each tree entry into a compact `sources[]` row ({sourceId, path, fileCount, findingCount, packsLoaded, warnings, coverage, ruleOverridesApplied?}) — the raw per-tree AnalyzeOutputView (nodes/scores/health/critical/ir/...) is never forwarded whole. WHAT THE COLUMN ABOVE DOES AND DOES NOT SAY ABOUT THAT, because this is the row where a defect hid: `analyzeOutputView`'s rows state what happens to a per-tree field in the `analyze_repo` reply, and TEST 3's key-literal scan runs over the WHOLE delivery lane (crates/summary/src includes cross.rs), so a `carry` satisfied by the join projection would read as if the analyze reply forwarded it, and a per-tree field's fate inside THIS reply is stated in prose here and nowhere else. Measured 2026-08-29: `nativeAnalyses` was `carry-conditional` on its own row and absent from every byte of the cross reply, root and `sources[]` alike, with nothing red. The structural half of the repair is `_replyRootKeys` below — every top-level key of each reply is now declared, so a channel the join drops (or lifts to its root, as `configWarnings`/`packsLoadedMeaning`/`nativeAnalyses` are) is a declaration rather than an inference, and crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs holds it against a real reply. The `sources[]` field list above stays PROSE and is the remaining gap: it names eight keys inside an array element, which neither the key-literal scan nor a top-level keyset can see. The raw per-tree output is available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

crossLayer.note: cross_repo shapes crossLayer into bucket ROW counts (`buckets.*` — one row per recorded call site), capped edges (`edges`, DEFAULT_EDGES_LIMIT=200, with `edgesTruncated` disclosure), and UNCAPPED DEDUPED bucket keys (`distinctBucketKeys`/`distinctBucketKeyFirstSites` — every distinct key, no truncation field; the 20-key DEFAULT_BUCKET_KEYS_LIMIT and its `bucketKeysTruncated` disclosure were deleted 2026-07-29) — never the raw CrossLayerResult object verbatim. The two views count DIFFERENT things, so `buckets.X >= len(distinctBucketKeys.X)` (measured on cases/: unprovidedConsumes 23 rows / 14 keys, edges 18 / 11), and the reply carries a run-invariant `bucketMeaning` sentence stating exactly that — the arithmetic is answered on the wire, not left to a reader who diffs the two numbers and finds nothing that explains them. Renamed 2026-07-31 from `bucketKeys`/`bucketKeySites` (pre-1.0 breaking rename, same precedent as census `sourceFiles` -> `parserDispatched`): a wire field's NAME must state its membership rule, and the old sites field was plural while carrying only the FIRST site per key. The raw edges/unprovidedConsumes/unconsumedProvides/unresolvedConsumes/externalConsumes/ambiguousConsumes buckets are available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding) and, since 2026-07-26, VERBATIM AND UNCAPPED from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane — plus as UNCAPPED IDENTITY (kind/key/bucket/source, no file or line) from the CLI-only `zzop manifest` lane (both in `_cliOnlyLanes`). The edges cap is why the manifest lane still exists: above it, two runs' replies agree on the edge COUNTS while neither can say which route left the join. Bucket MEMBERSHIP no longer needs that lane.

crossLayerFindings.note: Shaped via output::shape_findings identically to per-tree findings (total/bySeverity/byRule/byRuleMeaning/shown+truncated?+testPaths?+buildPaths?+note?+ruleMessages?+ruleMessagesMeaning?, with the same {shown, totalMatching, severitiesNotShown, hint} truncation object) — never the raw array verbatim. The prose fold applies here identically, one shaper feeding both lanes. Each entry of `shown` carries `message` as a string always; a text that MORE THAN ONE shown finding carries AND whose folding removes more bytes than the pointer, the `messageRef` field and the table cost to add is stored once in a sibling `ruleMessages` object (`{key: text}`, keyed by rule id, `<ruleId>#2` for a rule's later distinct texts) and those findings carry `messageRef` holding the key plus a short pointer `message`. The gate is net bytes, not repetition, and it is applied per text: a short message repeated inside one reply stays inline while a long one beside it folds, because the pointer plus the field plus the row cost about 260 bytes a finding and 45 of the 118 shipped messages are cheaper carried twice than folded once. Both `ruleMessages` and its legend `ruleMessagesMeaning` are additive-only — absent, never empty — so a reply whose every message is unique is byte-identical to what it was before the fold existed. The fold runs on `shown` AFTER the cap, is lossless (`crates/summary/src/output/rule_prose.rs`), and moves no count: resolve with `ruleMessages[finding.messageRef]`, never by parsing the pointer sentence, which `VERSIONING.md` keeps explicitly outside the compatibility surface while freezing the field names. One deliberate difference: no tree's `buildScriptPaths` is passed here, because a cross-layer finding straddles two trees and picking one tree's manifest would demote the other's paths on a name collision; the tree-independent half of the axis (anything under .github/, plus *.example) still applies.

warnings.note: ALWAYS written to `summary.warnings`, empty array included (`crates/summary/src/cross.rs`) — the same always-present contract the per-tree warnings/configWarnings fields already had. It was presence-gated until 2026-07-31, which made "this run self-reported nothing" and "this build has no run-level warning channel" the same bytes; the `.get()` on the SOURCE field stays defensive about older engine output, and its absence yields `[]` rather than a judgment. History: this row was the registry's first catch — when first authored, no delivery surface read the run-level field at all (the parallel-implementation-tripwire self-report was silently dropped), the exact shape this registry exists to prevent.

disclosure.note: Carried as a FOLD since 2026-07-29 (crates/summary/src/output/disclosure.rs): the reply gets the registry's counts plus a pointer (`zzop contract disclosure-classes` / `zzop://contract/disclosure-classes`), never the ~10.6KB of run-invariant prose. The full text is available from the contract lane on both surfaces and, verbatim, from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane.

_replyRootKeys._doc: EVERY TOP-LEVEL KEY OF EACH SHIPPED REPLY, declared. This block exists because the field rows above cannot cover the replies: their key sets are pinned to the FACADE VIEWS (surface_parity.rs TEST 1/2 make `analyzeOutputView` equal AnalyzeOutputView's pinned keys and `multiAnalyzeOutputView` equal MultiAnalyzeOutputView's), so a reply key that is not a view field — a projection (`sources`, `architecture`), a legend (`bucketMeaning`), a census (`buckets`, `coverageGaps`), or a per-tree field the join lifts to its root (`configWarnings`, `packsLoadedMeaning`, `nativeAnalyses`) — can hold no row, and therefore no status, and therefore no guard. That is a blind spot in the SUBJECT of the registry, not in its checks: the guards were green while a channel this repo had just built was absent from an entire reply. Measured 2026-08-29 on the nine-repo corpus: `zzop cross` carried no `nativeAnalyses` at the root or on any of nine `sources[]` rows, one day after the sibling reply gained it, and the only thing that would have gone red is a test nobody had written. WHAT `presence` MEANS: `always` = the key is on every reply this build produces and crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs asserts it against a real one; `conditional` = it may legitimately be absent (a cap that did not bite, an older engine, a phase that did not run) and only its unexpected PRESENCE is uncheckable — so the `why` has to name the condition. WHAT THIS BUYS: a new reply key is either declared here or the keyset pin goes red naming it, so `it is on the wire and nothing says so` stops being reachable by accident. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, stated so the next reader does not read more into a green build than is there: keys NESTED inside a reply (the eight fields of a `sources[]` row, the members of `architecture`, the shape of `findings`) are outside it — a top-level keyset cannot see them, and `multiAnalyzeOutputView.trees`'s note is still prose on that point.

analyze_repo._doc: The `analyze_repo` MCP reply == the `zzop analyze` stdout document, shaped by crates/summary/src/analyze/. SUBJECT: the TREE-mode reply, which is what crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs builds and what the `presence` values below are read against. The ENVELOPE lane (`analyze_envelope`) runs the same shaper over an input with no filesystem root, no config file and no git history, so it omits `path`, `config` and `architecture`; that lane is pinned key by key in crates/summary/src/analyze/tests.rs, which reads THIS BLOCK as its whitelist of keys the shaper invents — so a key declared here is declared once and both pins see it. Keys that ARE `analyzeOutputView` fields are governed by their own rows above and are not repeated here. HISTORY: these five lived as a Rust const (`SHAPER_INVENTED_KEYS`) until 2026-08-29, when the join reply needed the same declaration and a second hand list would have been the second owner of one fact; the const now reads this block.

architecture.why: Present only when GIT SIGNALS ran for this tree (`architecture_summary` returns None otherwise) — absent, never null, which is the distinction the always-serialized `gitWindow` beside it exists to make readable. It is the compact summary the reply publishes INSTEAD of the raw `health`/`recommendations`/`critical`/`scores` fields (each `carry-conditional` or `omit` above, with its own row saying so), and it carries its own `painMeaning`/`criticalTopMeaning`/`topRecommendationMeaning` legends as MEMBERS rather than as siblings — which is why those are not top-level keys of their own. Declared `always` when this block was first written, and a real reply said otherwise on the first run: the fixture has no git history. Kept as the block's own worked example that `presence` is a measurement, not an intention.

config.why: The config file this run honoured, echoed back (null when none governed the run). A request echo rather than an engine output, so no view has a field for it. Absent in the envelope lane, which has no config file to echo.

coverageGaps.why: The extension-level blindness census this layer computes, DERIVED from `ir` (which this reply deliberately drops, see that row) crossed with the census's declared-import side — so it is a shaper invention like `architecture` rather than a projection of one field. It ships ALWAYS, empty list included, following `queryCoverage`'s always-present `blindSpots` convention rather than `architecture`'s absent-when-it-did-not-run one: an empty gap list is a measurement, while a missing `architecture` means a phase did not run. See crates/summary/src/analyze/coverage_gaps for that judgment.

path.why: The analyzed root, echoed back. Same class as `config`: a request echo the engine view has no field for, and absent in the envelope lane, which has no filesystem root.

degradedTruncated.why: Written ONLY when the `degraded` path list actually hit DEFAULT_DEGRADED_LIMIT, carrying the standard {shown, totalMatching, hint} disclosure. Its absence is the honest `nothing was dropped` signal — the same conditional-truncation-sibling shape `edgesTruncated` has in the join reply, and the reason neither is an always-present null. The full count is never in this key: `coverage.degraded` carries it as an uncapped scalar.

cross_repo._doc: The `cross_repo` MCP reply == the `zzop cross` stdout document, shaped by crates/summary/src/cross.rs. Keys that ARE `multiAnalyzeOutputView` fields (`crossLayerFindings`, `warnings`, `disclosure`) are governed by their own rows above.

sources.why: The compact projection of `trees` — see that row for the eight per-tree keys a `sources[]` element carries and for what the raw per-tree view loses on the way.

config.why: The config file that defined the join, echoed back; null in paths mode, where no single config governs the run (each root loads its own, disclosed through `configWarnings`).

configWarnings.why: A per-tree `analyzeOutputView` field (its own row above) MERGED to the join root: the loader's own warnings first, then every tree's, in tree order. One config-honesty channel for the run rather than one per `sources[]` row.

buckets.why: Row counts for the six `crossLayer` buckets — the shaped projection its own row above describes.

bucketMeaning.why: The run-invariant legend for `buckets`/`distinctBucketKeys`, saying that a ROW is not the same thing in each bucket. A sibling key for the reason every legend in this reply is one.

distinctBucketKeys.why: The deduped key view of the five non-edge buckets, uncapped. Projection of `crossLayer`.

distinctBucketKeyFirstSites.why: One `file:line` per distinct bucket key — the FIRST recorded site, never every site behind it (`bucketMeaning` says so). Projection of `crossLayer`.

edges.why: The capped per-row edge list (DEFAULT_EDGES_LIMIT=200). Projection of `crossLayer`; the full count rides `buckets.edges`.

edgesTruncated.why: Written ONLY when the edge cap actually bit, carrying {shown, totalMatching, hint}. Its absence is the honest `nothing was dropped` signal, which is why it is not an always-present null.

packsLoadedMeaning.why: A per-tree `analyzeOutputView` field (its own row above) merged to the join root, present exactly when some tree loaded a pack. Merging is order-independent because every value is the same build constant.

nativeAnalyses.why: The native-analysis roster for the JOIN, derived at the root from the per-tree rosters and the join's own exclude-only gate (crates/summary/src/cross/native_analyses.rs). Conditional only in the older-build direction: the keys are `.get()`-gated on a tree publishing a roster, so an engine that predates the field degrades to omission rather than a JSON null. It carries a fourth key no per-tree reply can have, `zeroInCrossLayerFindings`. See analyzeOutputView.nativeAnalyses for the field itself and crates/summary/tests/cross_native_analyses.rs for the behavioural pin.

nativeAnalysesMeaning.why: The legend for the roster above, moving with it for the reason the two keys move together everywhere: numbers without the sentence are the half already judged insufficient. Two of its five sentences are read from zzop_facade's constants so the join and per-tree replies cannot disagree about the build fact; the rest invert by lane.
